value.name: Whitfield gestures Asha to sit
value.description: Whitfield, absorbed in reading, gestures Asha toward a chair without looking up.
evidence: he gestured her to the chair without looking up from the page in front of him.

value.name: Asha refuses to sit
value.description: Asha declines the invitation to sit and instead approaches Whitfield's desk.
evidence: She did not sit. She crossed to the desk,

value.name: Asha presents corrected filing
value.description: Asha places the corrected filing on Whitfield's blotter with Devin's signature facing him.
evidence: slid the corrected filing from her case, and set it down on the blotter so that Devin's signature faced him squarely;

value.name: Asha states Devin handled corrections
value.description: Asha tells Whitfield that Devin handled the corrections and keeps the document steady.
evidence: "Devin handled the corrections, sir," she said, and kept her hands flat on the edge of the blotter so the page would not shift.

value.name: Whitfield scrutinizes the signature
value.description: Whitfield studies the signature block carefully without picking up the page.
evidence: Whitfield's eyes moved from her face to the signature and back, and he did not pick the document up; he set two fingers on the corner of it instead
Whitfield did not pick the page up. He kept his two fingers on its corner and read down the signature block once, then again,

value.name: Asha waits under pressure
value.description: Asha remains still and silent, aware of the phone in her pocket and the weight of Rosa's words.
evidence: Asha held the room and waited, the phone in her coat pocket a small pressure she chose not to acknowledge, Rosa's last line still legible behind her eyes.
Asha held where she was with her hands still flat on the blotter's edge.

value.name: Asha rehearses her procedural cover
value.description: Asha internally frames her statement as a narrow, rehearsed procedural line while judging Whitfield's reaction.
evidence: The procedural sentence was out now and it sat between them exactly as she had rehearsed it in the elevator, narrow, accurate, survivable, and she watched him take its measure before she decided whether she could leave it that narrow.

value.name: Silence deepens the standoff
value.description: Neither person speaks as Whitfield keeps reading and Asha lets the silence work for her.
evidence: He kept his two fingers on its corner and read down the signature block once, then again,
Asha held where she was with her hands still flat on the blotter's edge. She let the quiet do the work she had not yet decided to do herself;

value.name: Copier interrupts the silence
value.description: The copier down the corridor cycles once and stops, briefly punctuating the tense exchange.
evidence: the copier down the corridor cycled once and stopped,
